autores.aporte: Describes work that becomes alien to the person doing it, along four distinct dimensions.

pregunta: Why can an activity that ought to express you end up emptying you out?

cita.texto: The worker relates to the product of his labour as to an alien object.

resumen: Work ought to be the way a person unfolds what they can do. Marx describes how, under certain conditions, it turns alien: neither the product, nor the process, nor even oneself is recognised as one's own any more.
desarrollo: Marx distinguishes four separations that accumulate. The first, from the product: what leaves your hands does not belong to you and confronts you as something external. The second, from the activity: you do not decide how it is done, so the hours are not lived as yours but as time surrendered. The third, from what he calls the human essence: the capacity to transform the world consciously, which ought to be the most our own, is reduced to a means of subsistence. And the fourth, from other people, who appear as competitors for the same post instead of collaborators in a common work. What matters is that he is not describing a subjective feeling of listlessness but an objective situation: one can be alienated without feeling bad, and feel bad without being alienated.
ejemplo_real: You recognise it in how people answer the question of what they do. Some describe what they make and some name a job title and change the subject. It shows up especially in work where you never see the finished result: you check one part of a process you do not control, for a client you have never met, and at the end of the day you cannot point at anything and say 'I made that'.
matiz_experto: The 1844 Manuscripts were not published until 1932, which split twentieth-century readings between an early humanist Marx and the scientific Marx of Capital. Althusser posited an 'epistemological break' between them that other interpreters reject, defending continuity.

visualizacion.descripcion_interaccion: A figure makes a complete object and the bond between them is drawn as a thread. The user applies conditions one by one — the product is sold, someone else decides the process, the task is fragmented, colleagues compete — and sees a different thread cut with each. They can restore them one at a time and see which returns the most: rarely the one they expected.
visualizacion.invitacion: Apply each condition and see which thread snaps
visualizacion.alternativa_textual: Four threads joining a person to their product, their activity, their capacities and their colleagues, cut one by one as concrete working conditions are applied: it shows that alienation is an objective situation with separable dimensions.

You do not decide how it is done, so the hours are not lived as yours.

parametros.resolucion: The four separations are independent: you can be alienated without feeling bad, and feel bad without being alienated.
